content.text:
I submitted index 26 (Ni 0.18 / Sb 0.82) as the best composition. It had an EQE of 0.097%, the highest of the three I could measure.

| Index | Ni fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | 0.34 | 0.037 |
| 26 | 0.18 | 0.097 |
| 28 | 0.16 | 0.089 |

- **Index 19** was my first pick because it matches NiSb2O6, which the MACE model finds stable. It performed worst.
- **Index 26** sits where NiSb2O6 should be mixed with an Sb-rich oxide, Sb6O13. MEGNet puts that oxide's band gap at about 2 eV, low enough to absorb the 3.2 eV light. I didn't use any XRD measurements, so the phase mix is inferred, not confirmed.
- **Index 28** was a little lower than 26, so the peak seems to be around Ni 0.16–0.2. With one measurement per point I can't tell whether 0.097 versus 0.089 is a real difference or noise.

Three measurements cover very little of the 29-point line. Nothing with more than 34% Ni was measured, and the gap from index 20 to 25 is also untested. I skipped the Ni-rich end because NiO is a poor photoanode material, and the middle because MACE says Ni2Sb2O7 is unstable there (0.27 eV/atom above the hull). Those are model-based reasons, not measurements, so a better composition could still be in the untested range. MEGNet's near-zero band gap for NiSb2O6 looks like a model error for Ni compounds, so I didn't rely on it.
